headline: Democrats won the House and Senate; futures rose while yields, the dollar and oil fell, Trump played down new Iran strikes, AMD and Insulet beat, and the put screen again passes nothing.
summary: The dashboard is a day behind: prices_as_of is 2026-11-02 and the Nov 3 close is missing, so every Nov 3 level here comes from Massive. On Tuesday SPY rose 0.30% to 754.35 and QQQ 0.62% to 685.28, which leaves QQQ 9.8% under its Oct 6 record close, just inside the 10% line. Overnight Democrats won control of both chambers (CBS, CNN, AP call on the House). Stock futures rose about 1% to 1.6% before the open, the 10 year yield dipped to about 4.92% and the dollar index fell 0.2% to about 101.7 (CNBC, FXStreet). Brent slid to about $102 after Trump said 'No' to new Iran strikes after the vote (Bloomberg, Dow Jones). AMD guided to about $17 billion next quarter and Insulet and NiCE beat this morning. All four 'Buy zone now' names stayed inside their zones on Nov 3, but no put passes the screen: NiCE just reported, Affirm reports Thursday, and the Microsoft and Capital One puts barely trade.

regime.why: Yesterday was risk off. The vote removed one big unknown and futures are up, bonds are rallying and oil is lower, so the stance moves to mixed. It is not risk on yet: the Nasdaq 100 is still near a 10% drop, the Bank of England may hike Thursday, Friday brings the jobs report, and Iran talks are not settled.

signals.title: Democrats win the House and the Senate: what changes for her themes
signals.since_yesterday: The result is in: Democrats won control of both chambers. AP called the House early Wednesday.
signals.what_happened: CBS projected the Senate for Democrats on election night, and the Associated Press called the House early Wednesday. CBS cites the AP count at 54 Democratic Senate seats to 44 Republican, with Alaska and Mississippi not yet called; those two races change only the margin. CNN projects Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats and 27 House districts. The new Congress takes over in January; President Trump stays in office, so he can veto bills.
signals.so_what: This is the 'Democrats take both' case from yesterday's brief, the one RBC saw as a modest negative before the vote. The market's first answer is the opposite: futures are up, likely because the uncertainty is gone and bonds rallied. Who pays and who gets paid: hospital and Medicaid insurers rose before the open on hopes that health spending cuts get reversed (Yahoo), and solar names jumped on hopes for clean energy tax credits (Yahoo). Defense lagged before the open (CNBC): a Democratic House controls budgets and oversight, though defense has support from both parties and contracts already signed stay in place. New laws need the President's signature, so the likely result is gridlock: more hearings, fewer new laws, harder spending fights and a higher risk of a government shutdown. Crypto rules not yet in law face a harder path. What would make this wrong: a quick bipartisan deal on spending or crypto, which few expect.
signals.for_you: Swing: let the open settle before any new swing; gaps on day one often fade. Puts: no puts on defense or crypto names this week. Long term: no verdict changes from the vote alone. LMT, RTX and GD stay 'Accumulate on pullback'; COIN stays Wait.

signals.what_happened: On Tuesday's close SPY rose 0.30% to 754.35, QQQ 0.62% to 685.28 and DIA fell 0.44% to 517.06 (Massive). Chips led: SMH rose 2.0% and NVDA 2.3%. Early Wednesday, futures rose: Dow +1.6%, S&P 500 +0.9% and Nasdaq 100 +0.3% (FXStreet); CNBC had the Dow up about 1,083 points (2.1%) and the S&P 500 up about 1.1%. Sources differ because they were taken at different times. The 10 year yield fell to about 4.90% to 4.92% (CNBC) and the dollar index fell 0.2% to about 101.7 (Reuters via CNBC). Before the open, Molina rose 6.3%, Centene 4.7% and UnitedHealth 1.4%, and the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) more than 8% (Yahoo). Tesla fell (CNBC), and defense and neocloud names lagged (CNBC).
signals.so_what: Bonds rallying with stocks means investors expect less new spending and fewer tax cuts, which can ease long rates over time. That helps expensive growth stocks a little. QQQ closed Nov 3 at 685.28, 9.8% under its Oct 6 record close of 759.66 (Massive), so the Nasdaq 100 is right at the 10% correction line, not clearly out of it. A one day pop after a vote is common; the real test is whether QQQ holds above Tuesday's close through Friday's jobs report.
signals.for_you: Swing: no setups on the dashboard on Nov 2 closes; wait for a close over a pivot on 1.5 times normal volume. Puts: the 10 year is about 4.92%, so that is today's bar for any put. signals.title: Iran: Trump says 'No' to new strikes after the vote; oil slips to about $102
signals.since_yesterday: Asked about striking Iran after the midterms, Trump answered 'No', and Brent fell 1.4% to about $102 by Wednesday morning.
signals.what_happened: Reports before the vote said US strike plans were ready from as early as Wednesday, Nov 4 (CBS). Asked whether he would strike Iran after the elections, Trump said 'No', and he told the Financial Times 'We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it' (Bloomberg, Ynet). Qatar says both sides are reviewing its latest proposal; an Iranian official called the US reply 'not convincing' and rejected 'excessive demands' (CBS, Business Recorder). One report mentions talks on Nov 10 to 11 in Abu Dhabi; only one source says so. Brent fell 1.44% to $102.11 and WTI 0.93% to $95.20 by 11:55 GMT (Dow Jones). Israel's leader reportedly pressed for more strikes.
signals.so_what: The Wednesday strike window now looks less likely, which takes some war premium out of oil. But Hormuz is still mostly shut and the two sides are far apart, so supply is still the scarce thing. A Democratic Congress is also expected to push back harder on the war, which leans toward talks. What would make this wrong: an Iranian attack on ships or another limited US strike like Qeshm.

signals.title: AMD guides to about $17 billion, while Oracle drops a $7 billion Tencent chip lease under US pressure
signals.what_happened: AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45%, and adjusted EPS of $2.09, both above estimates, and guided Q4 to about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, against about $16.2 to $16.3 billion expected (investingLive, Yahoo, Nov 3). It expects data center sales to grow about 50% from Q3, and took a $1.1 billion charge tied to customer warrants. Shares rose more than 7% after hours. Separately, the Financial Times and Reuters report Oracle cancelled a five year lease of about 100,000 AI chips to Tencent in Southeast Asian data centers, worth about $7 billion, after US officials raised concerns (Nov 4).
signals.so_what: AMD's guide says AI spending is still rising fast, which matters after a month of the market selling good news. The Oracle news closes a door: leasing US chips to Chinese firms offshore was a gap in export rules, and the US is now leaning on it. That moves some demand back to domestic customers and makes Chinese firms lean harder on local chips. ORCL closed at 126.19 on Nov 3, up 5.85%, before the news (Massive).
signals.for_you: Long term: AMD closed at 483.90 on Nov 3, inside its 476.31 to 564.60 zone (Massive), but its verdict is 'Accumulate on pullback' on Nov 2 data and it may gap up; no chasing. Swing: no AMD setup. Puts: none on AMD the day after a report.

signals.title: Earnings: NiCE and Insulet beat this morning; Remitly tonight, Affirm and Zoetis Thursday
signals.what_happened: NiCE: Q3 revenue $790.7 million, up 8.0%; cloud revenue up 10.6% to $622.7 million; adjusted EPS $2.84 against $2.78 expected; full year EPS guidance raised to $11.12 to $11.32; AI recurring revenue $392 million, up 46%; it also plans to cut about 5% of staff (Investing.com, AP, GuruFocus, TipRanks). NICE fell 5.45% to 106.27 on Nov 3 before the report (Massive). Insulet: Q3 revenue $842.0 million, up 19.2%, above its own range; international Omnipod up 31.7%; adjusted EPS $1.99, up 59.9% (Insulet release). One source says it raised full year growth to 21% to 22%; the guidance table was not confirmed. PODD closed at 154.86 on Nov 3. The stock reactions this morning were not found.
signals.so_what: NiCE answered the AI worry with numbers: AI revenue is growing fast and earnings beat, but cloud growth slowed to about 11% and job cuts say it is protecting margins. Insulet shows tubeless insulin pumps still taking share, and the overseas business is growing twice as fast as the US. For a clinician, the quiet point is margin: adjusted operating margin rose to 22.0%, which funds the next device.
signals.for_you: Long term: NICE stays 'Buy zone now' on Nov 2 closes and 106.27 is inside its 101.97 to 114.23 zone; wait for the first close after the report before acting. PODD is 'Accumulate on pullback'; a beat is not a reason to chase. Puts: no puts on AFRM or ZTS into Thursday's reports.

signals.since_yesterday: Forecasts for the Bank of England split: JPMorgan calls a hike to 4.0%, Pantheon expects no move through 2027, and the September vote was 6 to 3 with three for a hike.

cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. US debt is above $40 trillion, and a split government makes new spending and tax cuts harder to pass, which bond buyers welcomed on Wednesday.
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order: power in Washington is now split between a Republican President and a Democratic Congress. External order: the US is pressing on chip leases to China (Oracle and Tencent) while it talks with and strikes Iran. Technology: AI spending is still rising (AMD's guide), but the stocks are near a correction.

history.what: Democrats won the House and Senate in the Nov 7, 2006 midterms while the Fed had stopped hiking. The S&P 500 rose about 6.7% over the next 12 months (CNBC, 2022).
history.lesson: A split government did not stop stocks. The damage came later from credit, not from Congress.
